source_text:
γλῶσ σα λέγει ὥσπερ ἡ χεὶρ εὐεργετεῖ. Ἕτερον φωνὴ ῥημάτων, ἕτερον ὀσμὴ
κατορθωμάτων· ἐκείνη περὶ τὸν ἀέρα βρίθει, αὕτη φθάνει τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τοὺς ἄνω
πληροφορεῖ, αὕτη τοῖς ἄνω παρίσταται.
4 «Ἐπιλείψει με, φησί, διηγούμενον ὁ χρόνος.» Εἰ δὲ Παῦ λον ὁ χρόνος
ἐπέλιπε τὰ τῶν ἁγίων κατορθώματα λέγοντα, Παῦ λον ἐν ᾧ Χριστὸς ἐλάλει, ἐν ᾧ τὸ
πλήρωμα τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἐφίκετο, θησαυρὸς γνώσεως ἀνελλιπὴς ἐκέκρυπτο–
μέταλλον ἦν τῆς ἐπιστήμης, ἄνωθεν τὸν νόμον καὶ τοὺς προφήτας ἠρευνᾶτο, γλῶσ
σαν εἶχεν ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ καθάπερ ἐν ἑνὶ θεάτρῳ σαλπίζουσαν–, τί πράξωμεν
ἡμεῖς οἱ πτωχοὶ καὶ ἐνδεεῖς; Τί πράξωμεν οἷς ὁ λόγος ἀδίδακτος, οἷς ἀσθενὴς
γλῶττα, βραδὺς ὁ νοῦς καὶ ἡ καρδία ἀπαίδευτος, οἳ μήτε τὴν ἔξωθεν γνῶσιν
μεμαθήκαμεν, μήτε ἐλαχίστως τὴν ἔνδον γυμναζόμεθα;
5 Οὐκ ἔστι πολιτεία τὴν παρρησίαν ἕλκουσα, οὐδὲ βίος ἀντὶ λόγου
φθεγγόμενος. Πόθεν Ἀντωνίῳ τὸν χιτῶνα τῶν ἐπαίνων ὑφάνωμεν; Στεφανούτω
νῦν αὐτὸν ἡ τοῦ ∆αυὶδ κιθάρα· περὶ αὐτοῦ γὰρ ἐν κεφαλίδι βιβλίου καὶ τῶν ὁσίων
αὐτοῦ ἔργων γέ γραπται· «Μακάριος ἀνὴρ ὁ φοβούμενος τὸν κύριον, ἐν ταῖς ἐν
τολαῖς αὐτοῦ θελήσει σφόδρα· δυνατὸν ἐν τῇ γῇ ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ»· σπέρμα γὰρ
ἐκείνου τὰ πανταχοῦ τῆς Αἰγύπτου, μᾶλ λον δὲ τὰ πάσης τῆς γῆς τῶν ἁγίων
1
συστήματα. Ἐκεῖνον πατέρα καὶ γεωργὸν νομίζουσιν, ἐκείνου τοῖς τύποις τοὺς
ἑαυτῶν βίους ῥυθμίζουσι καὶ τὸν ἀπόντα διὰ τῆς φυλακῆς τῶν νόμων παρεῖναι
νομίζουσι. Λόγος εἷς τῶν ἐκ διαδοχῆς παιδευθέντων σῳζόμενος ἱκανὸς πολιτείαν
τὴν ἐκ φιλοσοφίας συστήσασθαι. Λεγέτω περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ Ἠσαΐας ὁ προφήτης·
«Μακάριος ὃς ἔχει σπέρμα ἐν Σιὼν καὶ οἰκείους ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ.»
thought_title: Tongues fail but deeds reach heaven
orientation: Hesychius confesses that his own speech is poor and turns to crown Antony with the words of David and Isaiah.
pass_a_gloss: A tongue speaks just as a hand does good. Voice of words is one thing, scent of achievements is another; that one grows heavy around the air, this one reaches heaven and fills fully those above, this one stands beside those above. "Time will fail me as I narrate," he says. But if time failed Paul when telling the achievements of the saints, Paul in whom Christ spoke, in whom the fullness of the church came, in whom an unfailing treasure of knowledge was hidden — he was a mine of knowledge, from above he searched the law and the prophets, he had a tongue sounding in the whole world as in one theater — what shall we do, we poor and needy? What shall we do, we whose speech is untaught, whose tongue is weak, whose mind is slow and whose heart is untrained, we who have learned neither the outside knowledge nor do we practice even a little the inside? [For us] there is no way of life drawing boldness of speech, nor a life sounding instead of speech. From where shall we weave for Antony the tunic of praises? Let the lyre of David now crown him; for concerning him and his holy works it has been written in a heading of a book: "Blessed is the man who fears the Lord, in his commandments he will desire greatly; his offspring will be mighty on the earth"; for his offspring are the communities of the saints everywhere in Egypt, or rather those of the whole earth. They consider him father and husbandman, by his patterns they regulate their own lives and consider the absent one to be present through the keeping of the laws. One saying of those educated in succession, being preserved, is sufficient to establish the way of life that is from the ascetic life. Let Isaiah the prophet also speak concerning him: "Blessed is he who has offspring in Zion and kinsmen in Jerusalem."

choices.why: πληροφορέω here is fill completely, not assure

choices.english: the fullness of the church came
choices.why: ἐφικνέομαι means arrive at or come to, not reach a goal
rejected: the fullness of the church reached its goal

choices.why: ἄνωθεν means from above, not from the beginning
rejected: from the beginning he searched thoroughly

choices.english: through the keeping of the laws
choices.why: τῶν νόμων is objective genitive of the precepts, no possessive in Greek

choices.english: the way of life that is from the ascetic life
choices.why: ἐκ marks origin, matching glossary ascetic life for φιλοσοφία
rejected: a way of life through the ascetic life

pass_b_english: The tongue speaks as the hand does good. The sound of words is one thing, and the fragrance of achievements is another. The one hangs heavy on the air, while the other reaches heaven and fills those above completely, and stands before those on high.

Paul says, "Time will fail me as I recount them" (Hebrews 11:32). If time failed Paul as he told of the achievements of the saints, Paul in whom Christ spoke, Paul to whom the fullness of the Church came, Paul in whom a treasure of knowledge that never runs dry lay hidden, then what shall we, the poor and needy, do? He was a mine of learning, and from above he searched the Law and the Prophets, and he had a tongue sounding through the whole world as in a single theater. What shall we do, we whose speech is untaught, whose tongue is weak, whose mind is slow and whose heart is untrained, we who have learned neither the learning from without nor trained even a little in the learning from within?

We have no way of life to lend us boldness of speech, and no life to speak in place of words. From where shall we weave for Antony the tunic of praises? Let David's lyre now crown him, for of him and his holy works it is written in the heading of the book: "Blessed is the man who fears the Lord, who delights greatly in His commandments; his offspring shall be mighty on the earth" (Psalm 112:1-2 [Psalm 111:1-2 LXX]). For his offspring are the communities of the saints everywhere in Egypt, or rather throughout the whole earth. They reckon him father and farmer, they order their own lives by his models, and they reckon him present though absent through the keeping of the laws. A single saying of those taught in succession, when preserved, is enough to establish a way of life that comes from the ascetic life.
Let Isaiah the prophet also speak of him: "Blessed is he who has offspring in Zion and kindred in Jerusalem" (Isaiah 31:9).
notes: Print divides γλῶσσα as γλῶσ σα, Παῦλον as Παῦ λον, μᾶλλον as μᾶλ λον; read as single words; gloss follows what is there with no invention.

problems.quote: Time will fail me as I tell my story
problems.why: Adds "my story"; διηγούμενον simply means "recounting," and in context (Hebrews 11:32) Paul is recounting the saints' deeds, not telling his own story.
problems.fix: Time will fail me as I recount them

edits.old: Time will fail me as I tell my story
edits.new: Time will fail me as I recount them

fixed: Fixed addition of ‘my story’: source διηγούμενον means recounting with no object, context is the saints’ deeds, so changed to ‘recount them’.

last_rejected.quote: then what shall we, the poor and needy, do? He was a mine of learning
last_rejected.source_quote: μέταλλον ἦν τῆς ἐπιστήμης, ἄνωθεν τὸν νόμον καὶ τοὺς προφήτας ἠρευνᾶτο, γλῶσ σαν εἶχεν ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ καθάπερ ἐν ἑνὶ θεάτρῳ σαλπίζουσαν–, τί πράξωμεν
last_rejected.why: Greek finishes Paul’s credentials before the question; English inserts the question too early.
last_rejected.fix: After the theater-tongue clause, ask what we poor shall do; then the untaught-speech question.
last_rejected.ruling: All content of μέταλλον...σαλπίζουσαν is translated; moving the parenthetical after τί πράξωμεν is a stylistic restructuring that preserves meaning without misleading readers.
